A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RT-PG research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments on Continuous Cart Pole, Swimmer-v4, and HalfCheetah-v4, including learning curves, sample-efficiency comparisons, runtime measurements, and sensitivity studies.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds Cart Pole experiments comparing adaptive and non-adaptive MPM coefficients.

M1.justification: The MPM estimator and RT-PG update remain unchanged. The revised divergence notation uses chi-squared plus one, equivalent to v2's exponentiated Renyi divergence. Algorithm 2's change from returning the last to the best parameterization reconciles its pseudocode with the best-policy rule already stated in v2's implementation prose.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three continuous-control environments. The new coefficient ablations use the existing Cart Pole task and input conditions; they expand hyperparameter testing without adding a dataset, domain, or distinct task scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix F.7 introduces Th-RT-PG, the non-adaptive coefficient configuration, as an evaluated comparator against practical RT-PG, with GPOMDP controls in Figures 10–11. The existing GPOMDP, SVRPG, SRVRPG, STORM-PG, DEF-PG, MIW-PG, and BH-PG benchmark comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added ablations sweep D over {0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8}, first holding N times omega at 32, then fixing N at 5 while varying windows from 2 to 64. These are additional evaluation configurations; the settings of the retained benchmark experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds a focused ablation of adaptive versus non-adaptive MPM coefficients and their sensitivity to D and window size in Appendix F.7. This directly tests a previously unisolated implementation choice. Figure 11 reorganizes Figure 10's results rather than supplying an independent additional experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report repeated trials with mean and 95% confidence intervals, and runtime means with standard deviations. The retained experiments keep their stated run counts. The new five-trial ablations extend the existing reporting practice without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 1–8 and Table 3's empirical values are retained, including the 2.11 sample-efficiency ratio for omega=2 and N times omega=32. New Figures 9–10 show broadly similar adaptive and non-adaptive performance at smaller windows, but slower non-adaptive convergence at omega=64. Figure 11 redisplays the latter results.

T1.justification: V3 makes local mathematical corrections: the Gaussian condition becomes sigma1 < sqrt(2) sigma2 instead of sigma1 < 2 sigma2; Equation 23 restores a missing importance-weight ratio; and Proposition E.1's derivation corrects the sign in the auxiliary Gaussian mean. The principal concentration and sample-complexity theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central trajectory-reuse contribution and complexity rates. Section 6 adds continuous state-action spaces to the qualifications on the fastest-known-rate claim, giving that central novelty claim a more restricted stated comparison scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F.7 adds interpretation of the theory–practice gap: non-adaptive coefficients can work similarly at smaller windows, while poor calibration of the unknown D may explain degradation at large windows. It contrasts this with adaptive weighting's stability. The existing dependence-on-D and dimensionality limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 promises code release upon acceptance; v3 supplies a repository and branch location and states that the code is available. V3 also reconciles divergence and output-selection documentation and specifies the new ablation coefficients and configurations. Existing hardware and benchmark hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works. Section 6 substantively corrects the relationship to prior methods: the epsilon-dependent batch requirement is now described as similar to earlier work rather than unlike it. Citations supporting vanilla-PG convergence are also corrected to Yuan et al. (2022).

P1.justification: Former appendix Facts C.1–C.2 are presented in Section 3 as Facts 3.2–3.3, and the memory discussion is rewritten and moved into Section 6. The remaining appendices are renumbered. Additional edits improve wording and cross-references and update affiliations, publication information, and acknowledgments; the overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: V3 consolidates v2's Tables 1 and 4 into an expanded Table 1 with memory columns and additional existing method rows. It reformats and relocates algorithm displays and adds Figures 9–11, including an alternative grouping of the same sensitivity results. The original figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V3 improves internal consistency through mathematical and implementation-documentation corrections, provides explicit code-access information, and adds a targeted empirical check of the coefficient choice. Appendix F.7 also identifies a large-window weakness of non-adaptive weighting. These are useful but limited gains: the principal guarantees and existing benchmark evidence remain unchanged, and the Cart Pole ablation does not fully resolve the theory–practice gap.
